skill.name: wp-migrate
skill.description: Guides WordPress migrations with wp-migrate.sh, including SSH push migrations, archive imports, backups, rollback, troubleshooting, and project development workflows.
skill.summary: Guide safe WordPress site migrations, archive imports, backups, rollback, and wp-migrate.sh development workflows.
skill.author: BWBama85

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, documentation links, placeholder URLs, sample configuration, and SSH option examples. Confirmed risks are operational guidance that could alter user systems: sudo setup commands, Git hook symlink installation, predictable /tmp SSH control sockets, and downloading WP-CLI without integrity verification. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or hidden executable payload was found.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes sudo commands for packages and system binaries.
remediation.suggestion: Mark privileged setup commands as manual-only and require explicit confirmation before any agent runs them.

remediation.issue: Pre-commit hook setup writes into .git/hooks through a symlink.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that hook installation is optional and should be reviewed before enabling repository-managed hook execution.

remediation.issue: SSH control sockets are documented under a predictable /tmp path.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp -d with restrictive permissions and remove the directory during cleanup.

remediation.issue: WP-CLI installation examples download executable content without verification.
remediation.suggestion: Add checksum or signature verification steps before making downloaded tooling executable or installing it.

content.value_statement: WordPress migrations can break databases, URLs, and files when handled manually. This skill guides wp-migrate.sh workflows for push migrations, archive imports, backups, dry runs, and rollback.
actual_capabilities: Plans SSH push migrations between WordPress servers.
Guides archive imports for Duplicator, Jetpack Backup, and Solid Backups.
Explains dry-run, verbose, trace, quiet, and confirmation options.
Helps prepare backups and rollback steps before destructive changes.
Troubleshoots URL replacement, table prefixes, wp-content, and cache issues.
Supports wp-migrate.sh development workflows, tests, builds, and releases.
limitations: Requires access to wp-migrate.sh, WP-CLI, shell tools, and target WordPress environments.
Cannot guarantee hosting compatibility without a dry run and backup review.
Archive support is limited to documented Duplicator, Jetpack Backup, and Solid Backups formats.
Production commands can be destructive and require explicit operator approval.

use_cases.title: Move Staging to Production
use_cases.description: Plan a push migration, verify prerequisites, run a dry run, and prepare rollback steps before launch.

use_cases.title: Restore From Backup Archive
use_cases.description: Import a supported backup archive, align URLs, preserve destination plugins, and confirm disk space requirements.

use_cases.title: Maintain Migration Tooling
use_cases.description: Modify source files, rebuild the script, run ShellCheck, update changelog notes, and prepare a focused pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dry Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a dry-run WordPress migration with wp-migrate.sh. Ask for the source, destination host, destination root, and backup status before suggesting commands.

prompt_templates.title: Import a Backup Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through importing a WordPress backup archive with wp-migrate.sh. Include format detection, disk space checks, URL alignment, and rollback preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Failed Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my wp-migrate.sh failure symptoms and logs. Help identify whether the issue is SSH, WP-CLI, database import, URL replacement, or wp-content sync.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Tool Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned wp-migrate.sh source change. Check build impact, tests, ShellCheck needs, changelog updates, and release notes before I create a pull request.

output_examples.input: Plan a staging to production push migration.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist with prerequisites, dry-run review points, backup confirmation, maintenance mode notes, and rollback readiness.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot an archive import that did not update URLs.
output_examples.output: A diagnosis path covering detected home and site URLs, search-replace settings, table prefix checks, cache flushing, and safe manual verification.

output_examples.input: Prepare a wp-migrate.sh pull request after editing source files.
output_examples.output: A release-ready workflow covering source edits, build regeneration, ShellCheck, test execution, changelog entry, and pull request summary.

best_practices: Start every production migration with dry-run and verbose output.
Verify database and wp-content backups before any import or replacement.
Use explicit user approval before running SSH, sudo, rollback, or destructive file commands.
anti_patterns: Do not run --yes on production until a human has reviewed the migration preview.
Do not paste real database passwords, SSH keys, or private host details into prompts.
Do not edit the built wp-migrate.sh file when source files should be changed instead.

faq.question: What migration modes does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers SSH push migrations and archive imports for supported WordPress backup formats.

faq.question: Can it run migrations automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide automation, but production commands should require explicit human approval.

faq.question: Which archive formats are documented?
faq.answer: The skill documents Duplicator, Jetpack Backup, and Solid Backups archive workflows.

faq.question: Does it help with rollback?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains backup locations, rollback flags, and manual restore procedures.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Typical workflows require wp-migrate.sh, WP-CLI, SSH, rsync, archive tools, and shell access.

faq.question: Is this suitable for code maintenance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes build, test, ShellCheck, changelog, and pull request guidance for the project.
